description: A correctly identified Judgment Candidate for material property treatment in thermal analysis.

candidate.question: Should material properties be treated as constant or temperature-dependent for this thermal stress analysis?
candidate.reason: The predicted temperature range (300-850 K) crosses a region where the yield strength of the nickel-based alloy decreases by approximately 40%. Using constant properties evaluated at a single temperature would not capture this variation and could lead to unconservative stress predictions.

alternatives.label: Constant properties
alternatives.description: Use material properties evaluated at a single reference temperature (e.g., room temperature or the mean operating temperature).
alternatives.tradeoffs: Simpler implementation and faster computation. May underestimate thermal strain at elevated temperatures and overestimate material strength, leading to potentially unconservative results.

alternatives.label: Temperature-dependent properties
alternatives.description: Use interpolated material properties as a function of temperature from the validated source dataset covering 300-900 K.
alternatives.tradeoffs: More physically representative across the full temperature range. Requires validated property data and increases computational cost. Interpolation accuracy between sparse data points introduces additional uncertainty.

candidate.uncertainty: The available property dataset covers 300-900 K but has only three data points between 700-800 K. Interpolation accuracy in this subrange has not been independently verified.
